# QS-PROC-09 Shot peening coverage (P2)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance and verification requirements for shot peening coverage applied to machined forgings processed on P2, line P2-L3 and associated operations that affect peened surfaces. It applies to production and rework where shot peening is used to achieve fatigue-strength improvements and residual compressive stress profiles prior to final machining or hardening processes. This document supplements process maintenance and operation procedures and is to be read in conjunction with MM-P2-L3-HT02, MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3, and SOP-P2-L3-03.

Requirements table
- Purpose: Record minimum coverage goals, critical control points, and referenced equipment conditions that are required for acceptance of peened components.
- Table entries:
  - Process step: Shot peening on parts routed from P2-L3 line
  - Acceptance criteria: Visual and nondestructive evidence of consistent coverage of targeted feature surfaces, no damage or deformation attributable to peening that would impair fit, function, or downstream processing
  - Critical control point: Equipment setup, media condition, nozzle patterning, and masking integrity
  - Related equipment condition: The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C.
  - Records to retain: Peening cycle log, media lot ID, operator identifier, masking verification checklist, post-peen inspection images, and disposition notes

Inspection method
- Rationale: Shot peening alters surface topology and residual stress. Inspection focuses on confirming a consistent and adequate peened surface while preserving part geometry and identifying any overpeening or media damage.
- Method overview: Inspectors perform a systematic surface survey of all peened faces using visual magnification and comparison to reference surface condition samples. Nondestructive checks such as surface topology imaging and adherence to referenced setup parameters documented in MM-P2-L3-HT02 and SOP-P2-L3-03 are used to corroborate visual findings.
- Steps:
  - Verify documentation from the peening operation: operator signature, media lot, blast cabinet or nozzle setup description, and masking checklist. Confirm that the peening operation was performed under the machine and process setup identified for parts from P2-L3 as recorded in MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3.
  - Perform visual survey under appropriate illumination. Inspectors look for uniform matte appearance and absence of concentrated burnishing, gouges, or embedded media. Compare to reference images maintained in the quality system.
  - Use magnification to inspect feature edges, fillets, and radii for peen-induced distortion or fracture initiators. Document findings with annotated images attached to the inspection record.
  - Where surface residual stress or coverage mapping is required by engineering, coordinate with quality engineering to perform the specified nondestructive testing and report results per SOP-P2-L3-03.
- Examples to illustrate judgment:
  - A uniform appearance over an exposed bearing journal that matches the approved reference image is considered acceptable when all documentation and masking evidence are in order.
  - Localized deformation adjacent to a masked edge that indicates masking slip or incorrect nozzle angle requires containment and disposition per the nonconformance handling section.
- Records and traceability:
  - Maintain peening cycle logs and media lot identification with the part route card. Attach inspection images and the inspector checklist to the part history file.
  - Retain traceable links to setup sheets and maintenance records referenced in MM-P2-L3-HT02 and MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3.

Nonconformance handling
- Objective: Provide clear, auditable steps to identify, quarantine, evaluate, and disposition parts exhibiting unacceptable peening results.
- Detection: Nonconforming conditions are identified through in-process inspection, final inspection, or field return. Examples of nonconformance include localized overpeening that reduces section integrity, visible media embedding not removed by cleaning, or peening on surfaces that should have been masked.
- Immediate actions:
  - Quarantine affected parts and mark routing to prevent unintended processing.
  - Notify the process owner and quality engineer. Preserve the peened part and associated fixture or masking sample to enable root cause analysis.
- Investigation and disposition:
  - Perform root cause analysis using documented media condition, operator setup, and machine state logs. Review applicable entries in MM-P2-L3-HT02 and MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3 for maintenance and setup history that may have contributed.
  - Evaluate whether the condition is correctable by rework without compromising part integrity. If rework is undertaken, document the corrective process, operators involved, and post-rework inspection evidence.
  - If the part is not suitable for rework, record rejection and scrap in the production and quality records.
- Preventive actions:
  - Where recurring causes are identified, update SOP-P2-L3-03 and the MM documents cited to reflect improved controls, additional operator training, or updated masking methods.
  - Implement changes to the peening setup or media handling only after verification and approval by process engineering and quality; document the verification results and update the records referenced in the requirements table.
- Records to keep for each nonconformance:
  - Quarantine tag and routing identifier, root cause analysis summary, corrective and preventive actions taken, disposition decision, and post-action inspection evidence. Link all records to the part history and the MM and SOP documents cited above.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L3-HT02
- MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3
- SOP-P2-L3-03

Notes
- This specification is intended to be applied in concert with the machine maintenance and standard operating procedures referenced above. Use the records listed to maintain process traceability and to support continuous improvement activities.
